newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says T-bill yields lower than expected.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says T-bill yields lower than expected.

text.p: Argentine Undersecretary for Finance Miguel Kiguel said Wednesday this month's Treasury bill auction fetched much lower rates than expected.
Argentina sold 250 million pesos of 91-day bills (Letes) at a minimum cut-off yield of 7.21 percent and $500 million of 364-day bills at a minimum rate of 6.75 percent Tuesday.
"The rates were much lower than we expected, much lower than previous auctions," Kiguel told reporters. He said yields are now basically back at beginning-of-the-year levels.
The last time 91-day peso bills were sold, in August, they fetched a cut-off yield of 8.50 percent. This week was the first time 364-day dollar bills were sold.
Kiegel said the low yields were a result of consolidation of the T-bill program which was launched earlier this year.

"I think there is renewed calm about the fiscal situation and that Convertibility (peso/dollar parity launched in 1991) will continue. The international market situation is also very favorable, where global spread levels are falling," he added.

Turning to debt, Kiguel said some $1.2 billion remains to be issued through the rest of the year. He said the Economy Ministry is still looking into what sort of issues there will be, but predicted they would probably be in marks and yen and some in the local market, rather than dollar issues.
Argentina's latest international issue was a seven-year 500 billion lira bond placed earlier this week. In September, Argentina issued 250 marks of 20-year bonds.
Kiguel has previously confirmed that a 30-year bond is one possibility the Economy Ministry is studying.
The other debt financing that remains in 1996 is the renewal of $500 million of maturing Treasury bills, said Kiguel.
